original_target.title: The sharp savings from junctions in planar connection networks

full_original_statement: For a finite set $`A\subset\mathbb R^2`$ with at least two distinct points, let $`M(A)`$ be the minimum total edge length of a tree with vertex set exactly $`A`$. Let $`S(A)`$ be the infimum of the lengths of finite straight-edge trees whose vertex sets contain $`A`$ and may contain additional junctions anywhere in the plane. Is $`S(A)\ge(\sqrt3/2)M(A)`$ for every $`A`$?
